_comment: PROVISIONAL GAME BALANCE, not engineering constants. These are the caps a
wallet gets when POST /wallets carries no explicit `policy` object, chosen
as a starting point, and to be TUNED BY THE OPERATOR through the game
config - Decision Ledger D8. Change them here rather than in code, and do
not treat a number in this file as load-bearing for correctness.
WHERE THE CAPS ARE ACTUALLY ENFORCED, because this comment used to send you
to the wrong process: max_per_tx and max_per_stage are enforced by
chain-svc, and max_per_stage is an ATOMIC RESERVATION taken before the
transfer is broadcast - wallet-mcp cannot see it, take it, or release it.
wallet-mcp re-checks max_per_tx and the allow/deny lists locally, but only
to give the model an immediate, honest refusal; it is a courtesy, not a
boundary, because wallet-mcp runs inside a persona designed to be socially
engineered and a caller can reach chain-svc directly. If you are tuning
these numbers and want to know what will actually stop a spend, read
Store.reserve in chain-svc, not the policy layer here.
Caps are DECIMAL STRINGS of whole VEE, matching every other amount on these
wires (ruled). An integer JSON number is still accepted on the wire and
normalised; a non-integer number is refused invalid_amount rather than
rounded, because a cap is an amount and silent-wrong on an amount is the one
failure this system is built to remove.
ALLOW LISTS NOW NAME CONTRACTS AS WELL AS WALLETS. The generic call op
checks an amount against the same allow/deny lists, with the CONTRACT KEY
as the counterparty - enforcePolicy is pure string matching, so this works
mechanically, and the consequence is a standing rule: a kind whose allow
list is not ["*"] must name every contract key its callers may pay
through. `org` is ["*"] and needs nothing; `agent` and `burner` carry
["*.{tld}"], which no contract key matches, so `converter` is listed
explicitly. Every future custom-contract key is added the same way, by the
PR that deploys it.
CAPS ARE PER TOKEN. `caps` is keyed by the manifest's token KEY, with
exactly two key forms and no globs: `*`, which is copied to every token the
deployment actually declares, and an explicit key, which REPLACES the whole
pair for that token rather than merging into the wildcard - so "au gets a
bigger max_per_tx" cannot silently inherit the wildcard's max_per_stage and
leave a wallet carrying two halves of one bound from two currencies. An
explicit key naming a token this deployment does not have is refused at
load, because a cap nothing will ever consult is a cap its author believes
in. A TOKEN WITH NO ENTRY CANNOT BE SPENT: silence fails closed here, since
an absent cap read as "no limit" is the one reading that costs money.
JSON has no comment syntax, hence this key. It is ignored by the loader.
